narrative.overview:
TrueTime Meetings is a darkened room where people's faces are the only light. The interface is the room itself: near-black walls, a few soft grey fixtures, and nothing that competes with the video. Colour enters through three doors only: the participants' cameras, state that needs attention (mic off, leave, live, warnings), and the company theme an operator picks. Everything else is greyscale on purpose.

Within that dark room the controls are friendly and calm. Buttons are fully rounded pills, the control bar floats as one soft-cornered surface at the bottom of the screen, and the brand face (Clash Display) is set throughout, so even dense panels read as one voice rather than a utility font. First-time joiners should find it approachable; regulars should stop noticing it. Density is moderate: a 72px control bar, 52px toolbar buttons, generous dialog padding (40px sides).

The system is a theme, not a single look. The same roles are re-skinned by eight company palettes (`black` default, `blue`, `purple`, `emerald`, `aurora`, `sunset`, `ocean`, `broadcast`), three of which paint a gradient behind the page. Every value below is the Black palette; components must read roles, never these hex values, so a theme swap re-lights the room without touching a component. The visual anti-reference is enterprise blue chrome: busy, blue-tinted toolbars of the Teams or Webex kind.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only (`color-scheme: dark`); tonal greys from #0A0A0A to #F5F5F5 carry all hierarchy.
People are the colour; UI colour is reserved for state.
Pill-shaped controls in a single floating bar; tiles and panels with gentle corners.
Clash Display for every piece of text; JetBrains Mono only for timecodes and figures.
Tokens and components come from `truetime-ui`; this app composes them.

rules.name: The People Are the Colour Rule
rules.body: Chrome stays greyscale in the default theme. A new coloured fill must mean a state (off, active, live, error, warning, success) or come from the operator's palette.

rules.name: The Roles, Not Hex Rule
rules.body: Style with `themeColors(theme)` roles or `theme.palette.themeColor[n]`. A hard-coded hex works in Black and breaks the other seven themes.

rules.name: The Tally Is Sacred Rule
rules.body: On-Air Red means live. Errors use Alert Red with an icon, so they are never read as on air.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Don't introduce a second sans. Text uses Clash Display, and only figures that update in place switch to mono.

rules.name: The Flat Room Rule
rules.body: Surfaces off the video are flat: no drop shadows on cards, buttons or the control bar (`boxShadow: none` on contained buttons and Fabs). Depth off video is a step in the grey scale.

rules.name: The Glass Only Over Glass Rule
rules.body: Blur is for surfaces with video behind them. Older dialogs that add a faint backdrop blur are legacy; don't copy them.

dos: **Do** take every component from `truetime-ui` first (`Button`, `Input`, `Card`, `ControlBar`, `ToolbarButton`, `VideoTile`, `StatusBadge`…) and pass translated text in as props.

**Do** style with `themeColors(theme)` roles and the exported tokens (`radii`, `shadows`, `motion`, `controlBar`); check every change in at least Black and one gradient theme (aurora, sunset or ocean).
**Do** use pills (24px) for call controls and page CTAs, 6px for controls, 12px for containers.
**Do** use the motion tokens: 150ms hover, 200ms state, 240ms enter, 180ms exit, standard easing; spring only for reactions and badges popping in.
donts: **Don't** hard-code hex, rgba, radii or shadows in the app; new tokens go into `truetime-ui`.
**Don't** add colour to chrome for decoration; a coloured fill must mean a state or come from the theme.
**Don't** use On-Air Red or Preview Green for anything but tally.
**Don't** drift toward enterprise blue chrome: dense, blue-tinted toolbars with many small square buttons.
**Don't** put shadows or blur on surfaces that have no video behind them.
**Don't** add a light mode, another theme provider or `CssBaseline`.
**Don't** uppercase button text; only status badges are uppercase.
